reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly shows that nanoclustering of Cr, Ni, Mn at grain boundaries reduces cohesion and correlates with ductility loss at intermediate temperatures in CrMnFeCoNi, supporting the core mechanism. However, the hypothesis adds a specific claim that low-strain cyclic loading accentuates this segregation, which is not addressed in the cited passages; that premise is unsupported by the provided evidence.
premises: Nanoclustering of Cr, Ni, Mn at grain boundaries reduces cohesion in CrMnFeCoNi
Such nanoclustering occurs at intermediate temperatures (<700°C) and correlates with ductility loss
Cyclic loading can accentuate elemental segregation to grain boundaries
Combined thermal aging and cyclic loading will produce higher grain-boundary nanocluster density than either alone
Increased nanocluster density will cause intergranular fracture and measurable ductility loss
